gaps.sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
gaps.hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
gaps.explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.

gaps.sentence: Please ___ me to post this letter.
gaps.hint: make somebody not forget: ___ somebody to do something
gaps.explanation: 'Remind somebody to do something' means to make someone remember; 'remember' is something you do yourself.

gaps.sentence: Her annual ___ is reviewed every April.
gaps.hint: fixed regular pay for professional work, usually monthly
gaps.explanation: 'Salary' is fixed regular pay for professional or office work, usually paid monthly; 'wages' are usually weekly.
'Who's' is short for 'who is'; 'whose' asks about possession.

gaps.sentence: Be careful not to ___ your keys on the bus.
gaps.hint: a verb is needed; meaning: no longer have
gaps.explanation: 'Lose' is the verb (opposite of find); 'loose' is an adjective meaning not tight.
'Lately' means recently and is typical with the present perfect; 'late' means behind time.

gaps.sentence: The new regulations came into ___ last month.
gaps.explanation: 'Come into effect' means to start being used; 'affect' is a verb and cannot follow 'into'.
'Valuable' means worth a lot of money; 'valued' means appreciated; 'invaluable' already means priceless, so it is not graded.
